articles.body: Sea-Intelligence has published issue 182 of the Global Liner Performance (GLP) report , with schedule reliability figures up to and including September 2026. Schedule reliability improved by 0.9 percentage points M/M in September 2026 to 50.6%. The marginal improvement comes after three consecutive M/M drops, with an aggregate drop of ‑14.8 percentage points, from a peak of 64.5% in May. The average delay of late vessel arrivals also improved, decreasing by ‑0.30 days M/M to 6.65 days. Despite this improvement, the average delay for late vessel arrivals in September 2026 is the second‑highest figure for the month. Source: Sea-Intelligence.com, GLP Report, issue 182 Maersk was the most reliable top‑13 carrier in September 2026 with schedule reliability of 64.8%, followed by Hapag-Lloyd with schedule reliability of 60.4%. MSC and CMA CGM followed with 57.7% and 51.8%, respectively. Wan Hai was the least reliable carrier with schedule reliability of 26.7%. Ten carriers recorded a M/M improvement in schedule reliability in September 2026, with ZIM recording the largest M/M improvement of 4.7 percentage points. On the other end, Maersk recorded the largest M/M decline of ‑1.8 percentage points. On a Y/Y level, none of the 13 carriers recorded an improvement in schedule reliability in September 2026, with PIL recording the largest Y/Y decline of ‑27.3 percentage points. PIL was one of twelve carriers with a double-digit Y/Y decline. Source: Sea-Intelligence.com, GLP Report, issue 182 In August/September 2026 MSC was the most reliable carrier alliance with schedule reliability of 68.9%, followed by Gemini with 68.4%, and Ocean Alliance with 44.8%. Premier Alliance was the least reliable carrier alliance with schedule reliability of 41.5%.

articles.title: Contship signs agreement to acquire Tarros Group
articles.summary: Contship has signed an agreement to acquire the Tarros Group through its subsidiary Sogemar. The deal will bring together two major logistics operators with established networks across Europe and the Mediterranean. The acquisition covers the entire Tarros Group, including its shipping, port handling and inland...
articles.body: Contship has signed an agreement to acquire the Tarros Group through its subsidiary Sogemar. The deal will bring together two major logistics operators with established networks across Europe and the Mediterranean. The acquisition covers the entire Tarros Group, including its shipping, port handling and inland transport businesses. Contship aims to combine these activities with its existing network to strengthen logistics connections between Europe and North Africa. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. Completion is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Expanding Mediterranean transport connections Founded in 1828, Tarros operates across 16 countries and 31 ports in the Mediterranean. The company employs 751 people and serves around 2,700 customers through its door-to-door transport network. The agreement includes Tarros S.p.A. and its foreign subsidiaries. It also covers Terminal del Golfo, Car Box, Compagnia Marittima Servizi and Med Logistics Malta. Contship plans to connect these operations with Sogemar’s intermodal network and its terminals in Italy, Egypt and Morocco. The combined activities are expected to support maritime and inland transport services along major trade corridors between Europe and Africa. Alberto Musso, Chairman and CEO of Tarros Group, said the agreement would support the company’s long-term development. “The agreement with Contship aims to create a Euro-Mediterranean platform by bringing together two major operators with complementary characteristics: a strong European identity on the one hand and a long-standing presence in the Mediterranean on the other,” said Musso. Matthieu Gasselin, CEO of Contship, also highlighted the benefits of combining the two companies’ operations. “We are convinced that the complementarity between its services, Sogemar’s intermodal network and the Group’s terminals in Italy, Egypt and Morocco will enable us to expand our offering and strengthen our presence along the North-South and South-North logistics corridors between Europe and Africa,” said Gasselin. According to a regulatory disclosure by EUROKAI , the purchase price is in the mid-double-digit million-euro range. The transaction will be financed through a combination of equity and debt. The companies expect to complete the acquisition before the end of 2026, subject to the necessary approvals. Further updates will follow as the transaction progresses.

articles.title: SC Ports secures nearly 160,000 containers of new business
articles.summary: South Carolina Ports (SC Ports) has secured nearly 160,000 containers of new business as part of its strategy to restore growth and strengthen its competitive position. The port authority is also expanding its focus on retail, manufacturing and refrigerated cargo. SC Ports President and CEO Micah Mallace outlined the...
articles.body: South Carolina Ports (SC Ports) has secured nearly 160,000 containers of new business as part of its strategy to restore growth and strengthen its competitive position. The port authority is also expanding its focus on retail, manufacturing and refrigerated cargo. SC Ports President and CEO Micah Mallace outlined the progress during his second State of the Port address on 27 October. He highlighted a 20% reduction in expenses, new commercial commitments and ongoing infrastructure improvements. The additional business covers retail, consumer goods, manufacturing and export commodities. According to SC Ports, the new volumes will gradually enter its operations through 2027. The port authority attributed these gains to stronger sales efforts, more competitive rates and improved customer service. Its cost-cutting programme has also helped bring pricing back in line with competing ports. “We are a highly productive port, with ample capacity, a customer-focused mindset and the market fundamentals to thrive,” said Micah Mallace, President and CEO of SC Ports. “We are perfectly positioned to achieve above-market growth, and we are now starting to see that momentum generate.” Recent commercial developments include a new transloading facility near the port for a global retailer. National retail brands and major importers have also committed additional cargo to Charleston, selecting the port as a gateway for shipments into the southeastern United States. SC Ports is also strengthening its position in advanced manufacturing. Inland Port Greer has attracted more business from companies seeking access to rail connections. In October, the facility received its first container associated with Isuzu’s new commercial truck plant in Greenville County. Industrial property activity around Charleston has also improved. According to Cushman & Wakefield, approximately 5 million square feet of industrial space had been leased in the market so far in 2026. SC Ports expects several major leases to support additional cargo volumes. Terminal expansion and rail connectivity SC Ports is advancing several infrastructure projects to support future growth and improve connections with inland markets. Work has started on expanding the rail-served North Charleston Terminal. The project is expected to create additional cargo opportunities in the short term while increasing container-handling capacity over time. Meanwhile, the port authority continues working toward the resumption of operations at Leatherman Terminal. It is also progressing plans to bring the Navy Base Intermodal Facility into service. Mallace emphasized the importance of rail connectivity for customers moving goods between inland manufacturing and distribution centers and the Port of Charleston. Alongside these investments, SC Ports plans to attract more retail distribution centers and refrigerated cargo operations. The strategy aims to complement its established manufacturing business and create a more diversified cargo base. According to Mallace, a broader mix of cargo will improve the port’s resilience and support growth across South Carolina. However, the port authority acknowledged that overall cargo volumes remain below previous levels. Mallace noted that port development follows long investment cycles, meaning the benefits of recently secured business will emerge gradually. “The business being awarded today will pay dividends for years to come,” Mallace said. “Momentum begets momentum, and we have started to generate ours.”
takeaways: South Carolina Ports (SC Ports) has secured nearly 160,000 containers of new business as part of its strategy to restore growth and strengthen its competitive position.
The port authority is also expanding its focus on retail, manufacturing and refrigerated cargo.

articles.title: Patrick Terminals launches digital app for truck drivers

The app provides step-by-step instructions throughout the terminal visit, including lane assignments and...
articles.body: Patrick Terminals has launched Patrick Connect, a new mobile application designed to provide truck drivers with real-time information and operational guidance during visits to its container terminals in Australia. The app provides step-by-step instructions throughout the terminal visit, including lane assignments and access to compliance information such as weigh-in-motion (WIM) results. It also allows terminal operations teams to send safety notifications and operational updates directly to drivers. According to Patrick Terminals, the platform aims to improve communication between drivers and terminal staff while reducing the need for in-person interactions. Drivers can access relevant information digitally as they move through different stages of the terminal process. Patrick Connect has completed a trial at Patrick Terminals’ Sydney AutoStrad facility and is now ready for rollout to transport operators. The company plans to onboard additional users over the coming months. “Transport operators are key to our market-leading landside operations. Patrick Connect puts the information drivers need directly in their hands, from the moment they arrive at the gate to the moment they leave,” said Bruce Guy, Terminal Manager at Patrick Terminals – Sydney AutoStrad. “It’s a practical tool that makes every terminal visit clearer, safer and more efficient,” he added. The launch forms part of Patrick Terminals’ broader investment in landside technology and digital infrastructure. Previous improvements across its terminals include automated gates, upgraded truck grids, truck management systems and digital booking platforms. By bringing operational instructions, compliance information and safety communications into a single application, Patrick Terminals aims to simplify information access for transport operators and support more efficient coordination between terminal operations and road transport. The company said it will continue investing in infrastructure and digital systems to strengthen the productivity and resilience of Australia’s supply chains.

articles.title: Fraunhofer IFAM Establishes Validation Chain for Autonomous Systems in Offshore Wind
articles.summary: With USD$9.87 million (8.85 million euros) in funding from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE), Fraunhofer IFAM is establishing a new research infrastructure for wind energy. The FOKUS-Wind project will create Germany's…
articles.body: Fraunhofer IFAM Establishes Validation Chain for Autonomous Systems in Offshore Wind Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 28, 2026 Fig. 1 From the laboratory environment in Bremen to the Offshore Drone Campus Cuxhaven and testing under real-world offshore conditions on Heligoland: FOKUS-Wind is creating a comprehensive infrastructure for validating autonomous systems for offshore wind energy. © Fraunhofer IFAM With USD$9.87 million (8.85 million euros) in funding from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE), Fraunhofer IFAM is establishing a new research infrastructure for wind energy. The FOKUS-Wind project will create Germany's first end-to-end testing and validation chain for autonomous systems in offshore wind farms across the institute's sites in Bremen, Cuxhaven, and Heligoland. The infrastructure will enable companies and research organizations to develop, test, and qualify drones, robotic systems, and sensors under realistic operating conditions. The aim is to support their reliable and cost-effective use for the inspection, maintenance, and condition monitoring of offshore wind farms. As offshore wind energy continues to expand, wind farms are being built farther from the coast. This trend increases the complexity, costs, and risks of operation, inspection, and maintenance—activities that already account for a significant share of overall electricity generation costs. Drones, robotic systems, and intelligent sensors can automate workflows, ease the workload of skilled personnel, and make offshore wind farm operations safer and more efficient. However, their widespread deployment depends on suitable facilities for testing and validation under realistic conditions. Suitable infrastructure for comprehensively testing these technologies under realistic operating conditions is currently lacking. FOKUS-Wind addresses this gap by establishing a large-scale, multi-stage research infrastructure that will enable autonomous systems to be systematically evaluated and qualified for use in typical wind farm scenarios. End-to-end validation from the laboratory to the North Sea The heart of FOKUS-Wind is a cross-site validation chain covering the full range of development and testing stages—from laboratory studies to demonstrations under real-world offshore conditions. At Fraunhofer IFAM in Bremen, a controlled laboratory environment will be established for investigating early-stage developments and interactions between robotic systems and different surfaces under reproducible conditions. This facility will serve as the starting point of the multi-stage testing and validation chain. The next stage of development and testing will take place at the Offshore Drone Campus Cuxhaven (ODCC). Opened in September 2024, the ODCC provides Fraunhofer IFAM with a testing and development environment for offshore drones that is unique in Europe. A coastal flight zone and dedicated flight corridors over the North Sea enable testing under real-world conditions. As part of FOKUS-Wind, the existing research facility will be expanded to include large-scale test structures. Plans include a nacelle simulator with a movable platform, a transition-piece mock-up, rotor blade segments with defined damage patterns, and a large-volume drone cage. The Heligoland site forms the final stage of the validation chain. The offshore island offers ideal conditions for demonstrations and long-term testing in real-world offshore conditions. Qualification, standardization, and certification - the path to industrial application In addition to supporting research and technology development, the new infrastructure will be available for education, training, and qualification programs. It will provide opportunities to test new workflows, train users to apply emerging technologies, and strengthen knowledge and technology transfer between academia and industry. The FOKUS-Wind team is also helping to establish the organizational framework required for deploying autonomous systems. This includes developing new operating concepts, integrating digital solutions into existing organizational and operational structures, and advancing coordination and approval processes among operators, service providers, and regulatory authorities. In this way, technical innovations can be developed and evaluated alongside the associated working and collaborative processes under real-world operating conditions. The test environment will also lay the groundwork for standardized testing procedures and future certification. Manufacturer-neutral interfaces, defined test procedures, and reproducible test conditions are intended to improve the comparability of results and accelerate the development of new systems. The project has already attracted industry interest and is supported by wind farm operators, industrial companies, certification bodies, and industry associations. FOKUS-Wind will initially run for four years. Thereafter, the infrastructure will remain available on a permanent basis to companies and research institutions as an open platform for testing and evaluating autonomous technologies for offshore wind energy and supporting their industrial deployment.

Join the leading maritime news network Photo: Wojciech Wrzesien/Shutterstock Four Romanian public officials and two other defendants have been indicted over the alleged fraudulent procurement of two tugboats that were supposed to improve navigation on the Lower Danube River but were delivered with drafts too deep for their intended operations. The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) announced Monday that it had filed charges against four officials from Romania’s Lower Danube River Administration (AFDJ Gala?i), an individual, and a company in connection with the €7 million project, which was financed through the European Union’s 2014–2020 Large Infrastructure Operational Programme. The two multipurpose, ice-class tugboats were intended to support navigation along the Lower Danube, including during periods of low water, and assist vessels in distress. However, prosecutors allege that the tender process was deliberately structured to favor a single supplier. According to the EPPO, the procurement specifications included technical requirements designed for seagoing vessels, even though the tugboats were intended for inland waterways. The requirements effectively restricted competition and favored one company. The vessels were delivered in 2021, but prosecutors say they failed to meet a critical contractual requirement. Both tugboats had an actual draft of 2.6 meters, exceeding the maximum allowable draft of two meters specified in the contract. Despite the discrepancy, the four public officials allegedly approved the vessels and signed final acceptance documents falsely certifying that the tugboats met the required technical specifications. The additional 60 centimeters of draft significantly limits where and when the vessels can operate safely on the Danube, particularly during periods of low water—the very conditions they were intended to help address. An individual and a company are also accused of assisting in the alleged scheme. Prosecutors estimate that the procurement caused approximately €7 million in losses to the EU budget, effectively putting the entire EU-funded investment at issue. The indictment has been filed with a court in Ia?i, Romania. If convicted, the defendants face prison sentences ranging from three to ten and a half years. The EPPO, which investigates and prosecutes crimes affecting the European Union’s financial interests, emphasized that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty. The case highlights the consequences of procurement failures in publicly funded maritime infrastructure projects, particularly when vessels delivered under government contracts cannot fully perform the operations for which they were purchased. articles.summary: The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach have identified liquefied natural gas (LNG) and methanol as the most viable alternative marine fuels for the near and medium term, with...

Photo courtesy Port of Los Angeles The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach have identified liquefied natural gas (LNG) and methanol as the most viable alternative marine fuels for the near and medium term, with a new study outlining potential demand and the infrastructure needed to support cleaner shipping at the nation’s busiest port complex. The joint Clean Marine Fuel Feasibility Assessment , conducted as part of the ports’ Green Shipping Corridor initiatives, examined which alternative fuels shipping companies are most likely to adopt, how demand could develop through 2030, and what investments would be needed to support bunkering operations. The study estimates that annual LNG demand at the San Pedro Bay ports could reach between 65,000 and 115,000 metric tons by 2030, while methanol demand could range from 64,000 to 250,000 metric tons, depending on market conditions and the deployment of alternative-fuel vessels. The findings come as shipping companies increasingly invest in dual-fuel vessels capable of running on alternatives to conventional marine fuels, although the industry has yet to settle on a single long-term solution. Approximately 4,000 vessels call at the two Southern California ports annually. Emissions from oceangoing vessels represent the largest source of emissions within the port complex, making cleaner marine fuels a central part of the ports’ efforts to meet their Clean Air Action Plan goals. “Strategic investments guided by this study will enable a growing market for these green marine fuels, helping ships serving the trans-Pacific transition to a cleaner future,” said Port of Long Beach CEO Dr. Noel Hacegaba. Rather than recommending large-scale infrastructure investments immediately, the assessment calls for a phased approach that takes advantage of existing facilities while supporting early adoption. For methanol, the study found that much of the necessary storage and distribution infrastructure is already available or could be adapted for marine fueling, potentially reducing upfront costs. The ports are encouraged to pursue pilot bunkering projects, provide incentives for early methanol adoption, and work with regulators to establish clear safety and permitting requirements. For LNG, the study recommends relying primarily on existing ship-to-ship bunkering methods rather than constructing major new storage facilities within the ports. The report also acknowledges that the environmental benefits of alternative marine fuels depend heavily on how they are produced and sourced. LNG and methanol can offer emissions reductions, but their overall climate impacts vary significantly depending on feedstocks, production methods and fuel supply chains. Fuel prices, regulatory requirements and commitments from shipping lines will ultimately determine how quickly demand develops. “Reducing emissions from ships is one of the most important challenges facing our industry,” said Port of Los Angeles Executive Director Gene Seroka. “This study gives us a clearer picture of where the market is headed and how we can work with our partners to make cleaner marine fuels more accessible.” The assessment builds on ongoing efforts to establish green shipping corridors connecting major international trading hubs. In April, the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach renewed their Green and Digital Shipping Corridor agreement with Singapore, with the partners committing to advance alternative-fuel bunkering, demonstration projects and digital connectivity. Singapore has already conducted methanol bunkering trials and awarded licenses to methanol fuel suppliers, while the Southern California ports have been working toward their own demonstration capabilities. The next step will be a joint request for proposals, expected by the end of 2026, seeking projects to demonstrate alternative-fuel bunkering capabilities in San Pedro Bay. The ports said the study will also guide future planning and coordination with shipping companies, fuel suppliers, terminal operators and government agencies as the industry works toward lower-emission operations. For now, the findings suggest that LNG and methanol are likely to play leading roles in the region’s marine fuel transition, with infrastructure development proceeding alongside actual demand rather than ahead of it. articles.summary: Fincantieri and ITS Academy Udine have officially launched the new “Mechatronics & Robotics – Smart Ship” program in Monfalcone, a technical training initiative jointly developed to train highly qualified professionals who will contribute to…
articles.body: Fincantieri, ITS Academy Udine Kick Off New Ship Mechatronics & Robotics Program Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 28, 2026 © Fincantieri Fincantieri and ITS Academy Udine have officially launched the new “Mechatronics & Robotics – Smart Ship” program in Monfalcone, a technical training initiative jointly developed to train highly qualified professionals who will contribute to the technological evolution of shipyards and to the integration of new technologies into production processes and onboard vessels. The launch ceremony was held at Fincantieri’s new training center and was attended by Paola Perabò, President of ITS Academy Udine; Alessio Belli, Fincantieri’s Head of Group Organization Development, Learning & Labour Cost; and Cristiano Bazzara, Director of the Monfalcone shipyard, together with course instructors, representatives of the Group’s Digital Lab and the 16 students making up the first class. The event provided an opportunity to present the training program, the related career opportunities and the applications of innovative technologies within the shipyard’s production environment. The two-year program, running from 2026 to 2028, comprises a total of 2,000 hours of training, including 700 hours of on-the-job training within the Company. Teaching activities will take place in Monfalcone, at the new Fincantieri Academy, and in Udine, at the ITS Academy premises, combining theoretical learning with hands-on experience and direct exposure to industrial processes. The program will develop specialized skills across the key technology areas that are transforming the shipbuilding industry, ranging from mechatronics to industrial and collaborative robotics, automation, artificial intelligence and Digital Twin technologies. Particular emphasis will also be placed on onboard systems and equipment, the digitalization of production processes, predictive maintenance and cybersecurity. The program prepares students for the role of Ship Superintendent, developing skills in planning, coordination and work progress management, alongside soft skills such as leadership, problem solving and the ability to manage critical issues. The aim is to equip participants with skills that can be immediately applied in the workplace, preparing professionals who can contribute to process efficiency and quality, systems integration and the development of next-generation Smart Ships. Fincantieri works with the ITS Academy system to design programs aimed at training specialized technical professionals, providing industry expertise, training activities, hands-on experience at its facilities and shipyards, as well as employment opportunities. The new program will also offer participants opportunities to join Fincantieri, including through third-level apprenticeship contracts starting from the second year, facilitating the transition from education to employment and contributing to the development of the professional skills required to support the competitiveness and innovation of the shipbuilding industry.

articles.summary: Boluda Shipping and Samskip have signed an agreement under which Boluda Shipping will acquire Samskip. The acquisition will pave the way for Europe’s most comprehensive short-sea shipping network, connecting Northern Europe with the Iberian Peninsula…
articles.body: Boluda Shipping to Acquire Samskip, Expanding Europe’s Short-Sea Network Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 28, 2026 © Boluda Shipping Boluda Shipping and Samskip have signed an agreement under which Boluda Shipping will acquire Samskip. The acquisition will pave the way for Europe’s most comprehensive short-sea shipping network, connecting Northern Europe with the Iberian Peninsula, the Canary Islands and West Africa. Boluda brings maritime heritage, a strong position in towage, an established container shipping business and expertise in port logistics, while Samskip contributes its established position in Northern Europe, its multimodal expertise, its customer relationships and its knowledge of the markets it serves. Together, their capabilities will support more comprehensive and efficient end-to-end logistics services, offering customers greater connectivity and access to more markets. The combined network will connect maritime, rail and road transport, with terminals playing a key role in coordinating the movement of goods across the logistics chain. Combining sea and rail transport with road services for the collection and delivery of goods can also help reduce CO₂ emissions compared with road-only transport. Following completion, the combined network is expected to comprise of 32 vessels operating 18 routes and connecting markets in 28 countries. Its 21 maritime terminals will link these corridors and bring maritime and land transport services closer to major centers of production and consumption. This network on land will be further strengthened by its five rail terminals and more than 500 company-owned trucks. The network is also expected to handle a total of 35,000 containers, representing annual logistics throughput of more than 750,000 TEUs. Building on the multimodal model that has been central to its development over the past decade, Boluda Shipping intends to invest in the combined network, strengthening capacity, expanding connections and laying the foundation for the next phase of growth for both companies and their customers. The agreement is subject to approval by the relevant authorities and fulfilment of the agreed closing conditions. The transaction is expected to close on January 1, 2027. Until then, both companies will remain focused on their customers, service quality and teams, while preparing to combine their capabilities and develop a broader, more efficient and reliable network connecting Europe and West Africa.

articles.title: MARAD Approves Deepwater Port License for $8.2b LNG Project
articles.summary: The Maritime Administration has approved a deepwater port license application for the $8.2 billion ST LNG project, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Wednesday.The project could further expand US liquefied natural gas export capacity.
articles.body: MARAD Approves Deepwater Port License for $8.2b LNG Project Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 28, 2026 © Adobe Stock/16th The Maritime Administration has approved a deepwater port license application for the $8.2 billion ST LNG project, US Trans port ation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Wednesday. The project could further expand US liquefied natural gas ex port capacity. President Donald Trump's administration has promised to ease permitting in a bid to speed up energy infrastructure development. The ST LNG deepwater port , set to be built about 10.4 miles (16.7 km) offshore Matagorda, Texas, will include four 2.1 million tonnes per annum liquefaction plants for a combined production capacity of 8.4 mtpa, the US Department of Trans port ation said. The project is still in a relatively early phase but some of its proponents have been involved in the development of other projects including New Fortress Energy's Fast LNG project. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with the port expected to come online in 2029. The location of the project is expected to move vessel traffic away from more congested onshore areas, reducing vessel collisions and safety risks, the department added. The US is the world's largest LNG ex port er with more than 100 mtpa of production capacity in service and close to another 100 mtpa under construction. The feed gas for the port will come from the Tres Palacios Natural Gas Storage and Trading Hub and the Williams Markham Gas Processing Plant through an existing Transco pipeline about 5.6 miles (9 km) northeast of the port . The approval comes about 10 months after Duffy announced that the Maritime Administration (MARAD) would take on oversight of deepwater port licensing from the US Coast Guard and streamline environmental reviews and accelerate license approvals. MARAD finalized the final environmental impact statement for ST LNG in just 410 days, nearly 3.7 years faster than the historical average, the department said, calling it the fastest deepwater port license review in more than two decades. The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration also on Wednesday proposed new rules to speed liquefied natural gas projects and expand ex port capacity. The Trump administration's pro-energy stance has led to a wave of public announcements from the largest LNG ex port ers, including Cheniere and Venture Global LNG, that they will move forward with permitting as much LNG capacity as they think they can build because of permitting certainty. Join the leading maritime news network Stock Photo: Garry2014 / Shutterstock U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) is demanding that a tanker reportedly carrying Russian diesel to the United States reverse course, warning its owner that delivering the cargo would violate federal law despite authorization from the Trump administration. In an October 27 letter , Blumenthal called on Greek shipowner Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Limited (EASTMED) to recall the Malta-flagged Agioi Fanendes , which reportedly loaded nearly 40,000 metric tons of diesel at Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22. The tanker was signaling the Port of New York and New Jersey as its destination, with an expected arrival date of November 7, according to shipping data cited in the letter. The demand marks a further escalation in the growing dispute over President Donald Trump’s agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to resume Russian diesel exports to the United States and global markets. “Should you confirm that this vessel intends to offload Russian diesel fuel at the Port of New York and New Jersey – or any other destination in the United States – we demand that you recall the Agioi Fanendes and to refrain from future transactions in Russian diesel in accordance with U.S. law,” Blumenthal wrote to EASTMED Managing Director Athanasios J. Martinos. The senator warned that delivering the cargo could expose the shipowner to legal consequences under the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act, passed by Congress in 2022 following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The legislation prohibits imports of Russian-origin petroleum products, including diesel. However, the Trump administration has issued Treasury General License 135 authorizing transactions involving Russian diesel through April 7, 2027, creating a dispute over whether the administration has the legal authority to permit imports otherwise prohibited by statute. Blumenthal argues that it does not. “We recognize that the Treasury Department issued General License No. 135 which reports to authorize transactions for Russia’s diesel exports, but no such license can supersede clear, unambiguous law,” he wrote. “The President may have given a license to facilitate this transaction, but only Congress can make it legally valid.” The Treasury Department maintains that the arrangement is legal, while the White House has defended the agreement as a measure to ease fuel costs amid supply disruptions caused by the war with Iran. In a separate public statement, Blumenthal said he was sending a “sledgehammer message” to shipping companies transporting Russian diesel toward American ports. “Reverse course while there’s still time,” he warned, adding that the administration’s license would not absolve companies of legal or moral accountability. Beyond demanding that the tanker turn around, Blumenthal is seeking detailed information about the companies involved in the shipment. EASTMED has been asked to identify the cargo’s seller, purchaser, charterer, insurer or protection and indemnity (P&I) provider, terminal operator, and any entity responsible for distribution. The senator also wants to know whether the company received instructions from the Treasury Department or any other federal agency regarding the shipment. The deadline for a response is October 31. The inquiry extends congressional scrutiny beyond the companies directly purchasing or importing Russian fuel to the shipowners, insurers and other maritime service providers involved in transporting it. The latest warning follows an October 24 letter from a bipartisan group of lawmakers urging major U.S. banks and port authorities to avoid facilitating Russian diesel imports. That earlier letter, signed by six senators and one House member, called on financial institutions and port authorities in Texas and New York to preserve records related to Russian diesel transactions, including shipping documents, contracts and communications with government officials. The lawmakers warned that companies participating in the trade could face future congressional investigations. The dispute comes as the first shipments begin moving under Trump’s October 9 agreement with Putin, which was intended to increase diesel supplies and ease soaring fuel prices. Under the agreement, Russia committed to supplying an initial 300,000 metric tons of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons thereafter. Reuters reported on October 23 that the Agioi Fanendes had loaded approximately 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low-sulfur diesel at Primorsk, citing LSEG shipping data. The identities of the buyer and seller were not immediately known. For shipowners and other maritime companies, the congressional pressure adds another layer of uncertainty to a trade that the administration has moved to reopen. Although Treasury has authorized qualifying transactions, lawmakers are warning that participants could still face legal challenges over shipments they contend violate the 2022 import ban. Whether those warnings will affect the Agioi Fanendes ‘ planned voyage to New York remains unclear.
